note: Initial portable counter slice for Phase P0. AMD/NVIDIA mappings are placeholders where equivalence is not yet formally established.

counters.semantic_definition: Kernel elapsed wall-clock time, measured in microseconds.
counters.normalization_notes: Placeholder duration fields from all backends must be converted to microseconds before derived counters.
known_non_equivalences: Backends differ on whether launch overhead and graph replay overhead are included.

counters.semantic_definition: Executed FLOPs proxy for the dispatch, normalized to a single count.
counters.normalization_notes: Estimated from instruction mix; treat as a proxy unless vendor exposes exact FLOP counters.
known_non_equivalences: Instruction mix interpretation differs by ISA width and precision mode.
Tensor-core and VALU/MFMA instruction families are not directly comparable across vendors.

counters.semantic_definition: Achieved throughput computed from achieved FLOPs and elapsed time.
counters.normalization_notes: Derived from achieved_flops; if either input is missing, this counter is unavailable.
known_non_equivalences: Requires consistent FLOP counting semantics before cross-vendor comparison.

counters.semantic_definition: Achieved TFLOPs as a percent of the selected target peak.
counters.normalization_notes: Depends on the target peak descriptor and active dtype/primitive.
known_non_equivalences: Peak model depends on tensor-core availability, precision mode, and sustained-issue assumptions.

counters.semantic_definition: Bytes read from DRAM (global memory) attributed to the dispatch.
counters.normalization_notes: Use vendor memory-byte counters where available; otherwise estimate from source/shape.
known_non_equivalences: Read counters are not consistently named or scoped as read-throughput across all profiler versions.

counters.semantic_definition: Bytes written to DRAM (global memory) attributed to the dispatch.
counters.normalization_notes: Use vendor memory-byte counters where available; otherwise estimate from source/shape.
known_non_equivalences: Write counters can include allocation or memcpy overhead if scope boundaries are too wide.

counters.semantic_definition: Measured DRAM bandwidth from bytes over elapsed time.
counters.normalization_notes: Formula uses decimal GB (1e9 bytes) for consistency with target peak descriptors.
known_non_equivalences: Different tools report GB vs GiB; use explicit source unit conversion before percent-of-peak.

counters.semantic_definition: DRAM bandwidth as a percent of target peak bandwidth.
counters.normalization_notes: Depends on target descriptor and memory-clock assumptions.
known_non_equivalences: Different vendors use different peak memory assumptions for sustained vs theoretical bandwidth.

counters.semantic_definition: Portion of memory accesses that hit L2 or equivalent shared cache layer.
counters.normalization_notes: If only raw hit/access counters are available, normalize to percentage.
known_non_equivalences: AMD and NVIDIA naming includes subtly different cache hierarchies and scope.

counters.semantic_definition: Average active residency of schedulable hardware units over the dispatch.
counters.normalization_notes: Prefer measured occupancy counters; do not infer from launch geometry alone.
known_non_equivalences: AMD wavefront and NVIDIA warp occupancy are not unit-equivalent measurements.

counters.semantic_definition: Active waves (AMD) or warps (NVIDIA) per scheduling slice.
counters.normalization_notes: Keep this as a raw utilization ratio not a percent to preserve source fidelity.
known_non_equivalences: NVIDIA and AMD use different scheduling quanta (warps vs wavefronts).

counters.semantic_definition: Share of time the tensor-core/MFMA/MMA execution substrate is busy.
counters.normalization_notes: Raw metrics are architecture-specific; map through this canonical concept only with explicit equivalence notes.
known_non_equivalences: NVIDIA uses warp-level tensor throughput counters; AMD exposes MFMA/LDS-centric utilization.

counters.semantic_definition: Number of tensor-core/MFMA/MMA instructions retired for the dispatch.
counters.normalization_notes: Do not convert this to cycles or time without an explicit model and clock source.
known_non_equivalences: AMD MFMA and NVIDIA MMA instruction taxonomies differ in width and packing.

counters.semantic_definition: Fraction of time vector ALUs execute useful VALU/SALU work.
counters.normalization_notes: Useful for scalar/vector balance against tensor-core and memory indicators.
known_non_equivalences: AMD and NVIDIA define VALU/MAC mix differently in their sampling taxonomy.

counters.semantic_definition: Fraction of time dominated by non-math scalar ALU work.
counters.normalization_notes: Proxy for compiler and unpack / index overhead.
known_non_equivalences: Scalar ALU naming and filtering differ by compiler and ISA.

counters.semantic_definition: Share of LDS/shared-memory cycles affected by bank conflicts or throttling.
counters.normalization_notes: Report as percentage only; do not compare raw cycle counters across vendors.
known_non_equivalences: AMD and NVIDIA define different shared-memory structures and conflict taxonomies.

counters.semantic_definition: Local scratch/spill traffic attributed to the dispatch.
counters.normalization_notes: High spill can indicate VGPR/SGPR pressure or aggressive inline behavior.
known_non_equivalences: Local memory spill accounting differs between stack spill and LDS/shared spill implementations.

counters.semantic_definition: Count of barrier/synchronization instructions in the dispatch.
counters.normalization_notes: Useful as a scheduler pathology indicator, especially for kernel shape and loop unrolling.
known_non_equivalences: Barrier opcode taxonomies are not identical, so exact equivalence is delayed.

counters.semantic_definition: Portion of cycles stalled on wait / dependency or memory scheduler events.
counters.normalization_notes: Use a narrow definition of scheduler-visible stall; memory-stall split should be captured separately when available.
known_non_equivalences: Wait/stall semantics differ by frontend availability and ISA feature set.

counters.semantic_definition: Average vector load width of observed memory loads, in bits.
counters.normalization_notes: Report the effective width after decoding instruction classes; treat as proxy when only partial disassembly exists.
known_non_equivalences: Vector width conventions differ for half/bfloat/INT payloads and compiler lowering.

counters.semantic_definition: Data requests observed at the provider's normalized L0/near-cache tier.
counters.normalization_notes: No gfx11 raw metric is currently mapped. A request is not bytes; conversion requires target- and experiment-specific calibration.
known_non_equivalences: Provider request and transaction widths differ.

counters.semantic_definition: Data requests observed at the provider's normalized L1 tier.
counters.normalization_notes: No gfx11 raw metric is currently mapped. A request is not bytes; conversion requires target- and experiment-specific calibration.
known_non_equivalences: Provider request and transaction widths differ.

counters.semantic_definition: Data requests observed at the provider's normalized L2 tier.
counters.normalization_notes: The existing MMQ mapping is workload-scoped and is not a generic byte conversion.
known_non_equivalences: Requests are not hits, misses, transactions, or bytes.

counters.semantic_definition: Data requests observed at the normalized last-level cache tier (AMD MALL/Infinity Cache alias).
counters.normalization_notes: No distinct gfx11 MALL request counter is currently mapped. Keep canonical LLC naming in normalized output and provider aliases in mappings.
known_non_equivalences: Not every provider exposes a physically separate LLC.

counters.semantic_definition: Data requests observed at the normalized device-memory tier.
counters.normalization_notes: No gfx11 memory-controller request metric is currently mapped. Request conversion and read/write composition require explicit calibration.
known_non_equivalences: Memory-controller request scopes differ by provider.
